title: Phase 5 — create ticfac and move
description:
Create the ticfac repo (PUBLIC, with ticks' scripts/check-public-repo.mjs guard copied over) and move: cloud/factory/** (~56k), cloud/sandbox/** (2,866), internal/factory/** (13,062), internal/cloud/{collect,lease,state} (1,250), internal/gatewaytrace/** (1,221), cmd/tk/cmd/{factory,cloud}*.go and tests (~9k), docs/design/cloud-factory.md, docs/factory-credentials.md, 16 repo-wiki pages, scripts/verify-factory-deploy.sh, the sandbox and workers-ai benchmarks, and the factory/sandbox/changes CI jobs.

DOES NOT MOVE: cloud/worker/** — that is the ticks.sh BOARD (D1 tickboard, ProjectRoom/AgentHub DOs, serves internal/tickboard/server/static). It lives under cloud/ and the naming misleads; the deploy-cloud release job deploys this, not the factory.

ticfac gets its own embedded.go carrying cloud/factory + cloud/sandbox; ticks' root embedded.go keeps only skills/. That file exists at the module root precisely because go:embed cannot reach above its own package, and it currently welds skills + factory + sandbox into one unit — this is the hardest structural blocker in the project.

OPEN QUESTION THIS EPIC MUST ANSWER: does the sandbox IMAGE (cloud/sandbox/*.sh) follow the factory while internal/sandbox Go and tk sandbox stay in ticks? internal/sandbox has 6,425 lines of Go test that literally EXECUTE those shell scripts, and cloud/sandbox/required-tk-commands means the container needs tk sandbox and tk cloud branch to keep existing — so tk is a RUNTIME dependency inside the factory's own container. Precedent for the direction: the Dockerfile already go-installs tk at a pinned ref from the public module proxy.
notes:
2026-08-27 12:06 - FROM TICK 46k: cloud/factory/required-tk-commands is DERIVED by a go/ast scan of cloudTkJSON call sites in cmd/tk/cmd. When this epic moves those call sites into ticfac, the scanner must move with them or be replaced — otherwise the derivation test keeps passing while scanning a package that no longer holds the calls, and the list silently stops matching reality. Tracked as its own tick (see the one titled 'The tk contract scanner only sees cloudTkJSON calls in cmd/tk/cmd').
2026-08-27 12:35 - PHASE 4 IS CANCELLED — no PATH dispatch will exist, so this epic owns two consequences it did not before.

1. THE SANDBOX IMAGE INSTALLS TWO BINARIES, tk and ticfac, each on its own. There is no shim. cloud/sandbox/required-tk-commands SPLITS: 'tk sandbox ...' stays a tk dependency checked against tk; 'cloud branch' becomes a ticfac command checked against ticfac. Two lists, each owned by the product that ships it. Note that cloud/factory/required-tk-commands (from tick 46k) is already the second list in embryo — it declares what ticfac needs FROM tk, which is the other direction and stays in ticfac.

2. 'tk cloud ...' DOES NOT SURVIVE AS A tk COMMAND. The twelve cloud subcommands become ticfac subcommands. Anything in this repo that shells out to 'tk cloud ...' — including the container's entrypoint scripts — must be repointed as part of the move, not after it.
2026-08-27 12:45 - FROM TICK ffy, and it interacts with the Phase 4 cancellation in your favour.

cmd/tk/cmd/cloud_logs.go and cloud_supervisor.go import internal/factory for factory.ReadSupervisor / factory.Supervisor. The ffy implementer flagged this as a problem — 'the one factory type a staying-in-ticks command depends on' — because at the time tk cloud was expected to stay.

It no longer does. Phase 4 is cancelled and the twelve tk cloud subcommands become ticfac subcommands, so both files leave with the factory and the supervisor edge goes with them. No plan needed for factory.Supervisor; just do not leave those two files behind.

MEASURED COST OF NOT DOING THIS EARLIER, for context on why deferring was right: factory code costs a tk build 163KB (0.72%) at the dashboard edge, or 2.07MB (9.1%) for the whole tk factory family, and 4 packages of 337 in the dependency closure with ZERO third-party modules. Compile time shows no signal. Nothing here justified a build-tag scheme ahead of the move.

ALSO BUDGET FOR: ResetFlags in cmd/tk/cmd/root.go is a hand-maintained list of every command's flag variables. Removing command files breaks the build there and nowhere else — a test helper, fixed by deleting the corresponding lines. The wiki previously claimed removal took zero edits elsewhere; that was wrong and is corrected.
2026-09-01 10:06 - READINESS CHECK BEFORE PLANNING (2026-09-01). Phase 5 is NOT a file move yet. There is a decoupling tranche first, and it exists because the plan changed underneath Phase 1.

WHAT PHASE 1 ACTUALLY CLEANED: internal/factory/**, internal/cloud/** and internal/gatewaytrace/**. Those are clean — they import only the factory's own packages plus internal/factory/credentials.

WHAT IT DID NOT CLEAN: cmd/tk/cmd/cloud*.go and factory*.go. At the time those were STAYING in ticks, because the plan then had tk dispatching 'tk factory ...' to an external binary. Peter cancelled that on 2026-08-28 — ticfac is its own binary — so those ~23 command files now LEAVE, and every ticks package they import becomes a cross-repo import of an internal/ package, which Go forbids outright.

THE FIVE REMAINING EDGES, all from the command files:
  internal/tick        cloud_test.go, cloud_tk_test.go, cloud_wave_test.go — TESTS ONLY. The tracker. Should become tk CLI calls, the same answer Phase 1 gave for the non-test sites.
  internal/github      cloud.go, cloud_wave.go — copy it, as tick psh already did for internal/factory. Do NOT promote: it handles OAuth device-flow token exchange.
  internal/tui         factory_dashboard.go — shared TUI scaffolding. Copy or let ticfac own its own, same reasoning as the palette decision.
  internal/herd/config cloud_wave.go — reads .tick/runners.toml. NOTE: contracts/runners-config-contract.json now pins that format across languages, so this one has a contract-shaped answer rather than a copy-shaped one.
  internal/sandbox     cloud_branch.go, cloud_inrun.go — and this is the knot the spec already flagged: internal/sandbox STAYS in ticks (herd_spawn uses it), while cloud/sandbox/*.sh moves. The command files that bridge them leave. Decide this deliberately; it is the one edge with no obvious right answer.

SO THE PHASE HAS TWO TRANCHES: cut these five edges while everything is still in one tree and one test run can prove it, THEN move. Same ordering discipline that made Phase 1 and Phase 4b work — do the hard change while both halves are still in one place.

Do not treat this as a defect in Phase 1. Its acceptance was written against the plan of the day and it met it; the plan changed afterwards, which is exactly why this check happened before planning rather than during the move.
acceptance_criteria: Both repos green. tk factory deploy works from the new binary against a real Cloudflare account. A sandbox image builds and its required-tk-commands check passes. ticks' embedded.go carries only skills/. No factory file remains in ticks and no ticks internal/ import remains in ticfac. The sandbox-image question is answered in writing with its reasoning.
